explanation: Track the highest bar seen from each end. Resolve the side with the smaller known boundary: that side’s maximum fixes its water level because the opposite side already provides a sufficient boundary.
timeComplexity: O(n) Each iteration resolves and advances one end position.
spaceComplexity: O(1) Only end indices, maxima and the total are stored.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: At each step the side with the smaller known maximum can be resolved: the opposite maximum already provides a sufficient retaining boundary. The water above that bar is the known side maximum minus its height. Every position is resolved once, so summing those contributions gives all trapped rainwater.
walkthrough: For [3,0,2,0,4], the interior cells hold 3, 1 and 3 units below level 3. End bars hold none, giving total 7.
edgeCases: Empty or monotone histograms trap no water.
A lower interior bar contributes more water beneath the same boundaries.
This sums water across bars rather than choosing one container pair.
